label: H.R. 3869

selection.reason: Impact scored and summarised by Gemini.

summary: H.R. 3869, titled the 'Every Veteran Housed Act', amends title 38 of the United States Code to expand who qualifies for homelessness benefits administered by the Secretary of Veterans Affairs. It updates the definition of a veteran to include individuals discharged or released from the uniformed services under conditions other than dishonorable or general court-martial, regardless of length of service or other previous service restrictions.

affected_groups.effect: Gain expanded eligibility for Department of Veterans Affairs homelessness benefits if they were discharged under conditions other than dishonorable or general court-martial, regardless of length or type of service.
affected_groups.group: Former members of the uniformed services

key_provisions: Expands the legal definition of 'veteran' for homelessness benefits to include those discharged under conditions other than dishonorable or general court-martial.
Makes eligibility independent of the length of the period of service.
Applies eligibility regardless of whether the individual was in an active or reserve component, or whether the service was active duty.
Allows eligibility regardless of whether the person currently serves in the uniformed services.
Makes eligibility independent of whether a person had a prior discharge under dishonorable or general court-martial conditions during a different period of service.
Removes subsection (b) from section 2002 of title 38 and updates related minimum active-duty service requirements for chapter 20 programs.

summary_detail.plain_summary: H.R. 3869, titled the 'Every Veteran Housed Act', amends title 38 of the United States Code to expand who qualifies for homelessness benefits administered by the Secretary of Veterans Affairs. It updates the definition of a veteran to include individuals discharged or released from the uniformed services under conditions other than dishonorable or general court-martial, regardless of length of service or other previous service restrictions.
summary_detail.significance: The bill broadens access to federal VA homelessness benefits by removing previous restrictions related to length of service, active versus reserve status, and other service conditions. The source text does not provide data on the exact number of individuals who would become newly eligible, the cost of implementation, or administrative changes.
